nodes.title: Tate variants with the necessary quantifiers
nodes.statement: Retain MC.7/tate-conjecture, MC.7/strong-tate-conjecture and MC.7/tate-beilinson-conjecture. For k finitely generated over its prime field and l≠char(k), T(X,p,l) says CH^p(X)⊗Q_l→H^{2p}(X_ksep,Q_l(p))^{G_k} is onto. The geometric Tate subspace is the union of invariants for open subgroups, equivalently classes defined after finite extension; it is a different target. Strong Tate also requires the invariants to be a direct summand of the G_k-representation. Over a finite field, Tate–Beilinson combines this Q_l-surjectivity with injectivity of CH^p(X)⊗Q→H^{2p}(X_ksep,Q_l(p)); its injectivity uses rational Chow coefficients, with no claim here of Q_l-linear injectivity. Global strong Tate over all smooth projective varieties and relevant powers yields the Lefschetz/Künneth/numerical standard conjectures in the stated theory; no implication to Hodge positivity in positive characteristic is asserted. Integral Z_l surjectivity is a distinct generally false strengthening. Preserve also the inherited variants with their hypotheses: the Borel–Moore cycle-class conjecture for an arbitrary variety over a finitely generated field follows from the smooth-projective version if it admits a resolution with smooth compactification; over finite fields divisor Tate implies integral divisor Tate, and divisor Tate for all surfaces over finite fields implies integral1-cycle Tate over their algebraic closures. For a smooth projective surface over a finite field fibred with connected fibres over a smooth projective curve and smooth generic fibre of Jacobian J, divisor Tate is equivalent to finite Brauer group, finite Sha(J), and BSD for J over the function field. These implications import the exact arithmetic proof contracts in G-TATE-VARIANTS.

nodes.title: Bloch–Beilinson filtration in Jannsen’s version 1
nodes.statement: For a field k and one fixed classical Weil cohomology H, a version-1 Bloch–Beilinson system assigns a descending Q-subspace filtration F^ν CH^j(X)_Q for every smooth projective X/k and j≥0. It has F^0=CH^j_Q, F^1=ker(cl_H), products F^r·F^s⊆F^{r+s}, and compatibility with pullback and proper pushforward with their codimension shifts. Assuming rational algebraic Künneth C for the system, the induced action on Gr_F^ν CH^j depends only on homological correspondence classes and π_i acts as δ_{i,2j-ν}. For each (X,j) the filtration is eventually zero. The strong form requires F^{j+1}=0. Existence is a global conjecture, not a chosen axiom on individual Chow groups.

nodes.title: Murre’s conjecture and its filtration
nodes.statement: For each irreducible smooth projective d-fold X/k and a fixed Weil cohomology, Murre data consist of rational Chow correspondences π_0,…,π_{2d} lifting the cohomological projectors, with π_iπ_j=0 for i≠j, π_i²=π_i and sum π_i=Δ_X in CH^d(X×X)_Q. Require π_{2j+1},…,π_{2d} to kill CH^j_Q; put F^ν CH^j_Q=intersection_{r=0}^{ν-1} ker(π_{2j-r}) with π_i=0 for indices outside [0,2d]; require independence from the chosen projectors and F^1=CH^j_hom,Q. The strong form additionally makes π_0,…,π_{j-1} act as zero. The conjecture is existence of these data and laws for every X, with the corresponding choice-independent system.

nodes.title: Motivic t-structure relative to a realization
nodes.statement: Let k be a perfect field admitting resolution of singularities (in particular a characteristic-zero field) and DM_gm(k,Q) the rational idempotent-complete triangulated rigid tensor category supplied by MC.4. Fix a tensor triangulated Betti realization to D^b(Vec_Q) when k embeds in C, or geometric l-adic realization to D^b(Vec_Q_l), l≠char(k). A motivic t-structure μ is a Mathlib t-structure on this category whose cohomology is conservative (nondegenerate in Beilinson’s stated sense), whose unit belongs to the heart and whose tensor product satisfies μ^{≤a}⊗μ^{≤b}⊂μ^{≤a+b} and μ^{≥a}⊗μ^{≥b}⊂μ^{≥a+b} for all integers a,b, and for which the chosen realization is t-exact. Tensoring with a heart object is therefore t-exact; arbitrary shifted objects do not define t-exact tensor functors. Its heart is exactly μ^{≤0}∩μ^{≥0}. The conjecture asserts existence. Boundedness, uniqueness and Tannakian properties are consequences under this premise, not fields asserting that an arbitrary triangulated category is already abelian.

nodes.statement: Under S3 write φ=ψ∘cl:CH₁(X)→M. A topological obstruction means ψ is not onto. Over the real numbers a Hodge obstruction means ψ is onto but ψ restricted to Hdg_G^{2d−2}{}_0 is not onto. Over the real numbers a cycle obstruction means that restricted map is onto but φ is not. Over a general real closed field with H²(O)=0, a cycle obstruction means ψ is onto but φ is not. These predicates classify failures of the detector φ, not every possible failure of real IHC. In particular φ onto need not imply real IHC without the hypotheses of the descent criterion below.

nodes.title: Algebraic curves, Picard torsion and even genus
nodes.statement: Under S3 assume H²(X,O_X)=0 and real IHC for 1-cycles. Then cl_R(CH₁(X))⊂H^{d−1}(X(R),F₂) and cl_R(Pic(X)[2∞])⊂H¹(X(R),F₂) are exact orthogonal complements. If in addition d≥2 or X(R)=∅, X contains a geometrically integral curve of even geometric genus if and only if Pic(X)[2∞]→Pic(XC)^G[2∞] is onto. The additional dimension-or-emptiness condition corrects the unqualified printed assertion: a positive-real-point odd-genus curve is a counterexample in dimension 1. If Pic(XC)[2]=0, the Borel–Haefliger curve map is onto and an even-genus curve exists; in dimension 1 the torsion-free Picard hypothesis forces genus 0.

nodes.title: Geometric-genus-zero surfaces and Enriques curves

For an Enriques surface, geometric 2-primary Picard torsion is generated by the descended canonical class, so an even-genus curve exists over every real closed field. nodes.title: Obstruction to the displayed Campedelli descent
nodes.statement: Let ζ be primitive of order8 and f[x₀:…:x₆]=[ζ x̄₁:x̄₀:ζ² x̄₃:x̄₂:ζ³ x̄₅:x̄₄:x̄₆]. Then g=f² has weights(1,7,2,6,3,5,0) modulo8 and f has order16. On quadrics set T(Q)=overline(Q(f(x))); this is conjugate-linear and T²=g*. Quadratic weight spaces of even weight have dimension 4 and of odd weight dimension 3. On the weight 4 basis(a,b,c,d)=(x₀x₄,x₁x₅,x₂²,x₃²), T(Aa+Bb+Cc+Dd)=B̄a−Āb+D̄c−C̄d, so T²=-1 and there is no T-stable complex line. Consequently a scheme-theoretic smooth complete intersection Y of nonzero quadrics Q_i of weights2i, i=0,1,2,3, cannot be f-stable: its quadratic ideal has weight 4 part C Q₂, which would have to be T-stable. Thus this displayed construction cannot supply the claimed real Campedelli example. Existence of a replacement real-empty surface with H^i(O)=0 for i>0 and failed torsion descent remains a gap.

nodes.title: Quartic K3 surfaces with Hodge obstructions
nodes.statement: The two Example 4.5–4.6 families are source-scoped existence targets over the real numbers. In an empty-real-locus very general quartic with Pic(XC)=Z·h, a smooth hyperplane section has genus 3 and hence detector0. Since CH₁ is generated by the hyperplane class, the detector vanishes on all cycles; the genus-detector theorem then excludes every geometrically integral even-geometric-genus curve. This argument does not identify arithmetic and geometric genus for singular curves. Both fail the corresponding detector through a Hodge obstruction. Existence of the required very-general real fibers and Picard-rank statements is a Noether–Lefschetz/deformation input recorded as a gap.

nodes.title: Valuation and specialization obstruction in quartic fibrations
nodes.statement: Over kbar((t)) with kbar an algebraic closure of a finite field, the quartic x₀⁴+t x₁⁴+t²x₂⁴+t³x₃⁴=0 has no point over an odd-degree finite extension: after a valuation extension of odd ramification index e, the nonzero term valuations are distinct modulo4. Consequently the quartic-fibration construction of Examples4.7–4.8 has every complex curve of even projection degree. The special bidegree(4,4) equation over P¹ is v(u³x₀⁴+u²v x₁⁴+uv²x₂⁴+v³x₃⁴)=0; specialize curves to it and use the generic-fiber valuation obstruction. Smooth real approximations over P¹_R can have a real section whose topological projection is nonzero while every algebraic curve has zero mod-2 projection. Over an empty-real conic B, the corresponding smooth approximation has every geometrically integral curve of odd genus by the finite-cover parity criterion, hence ind₁=2. These yield cycle obstructions. The real approximation and DVR cycle specialization contracts, rather than normal-cone specialization, are required inputs.

nodes.title: Unramified description of the torsion 1-cycle defect
nodes.statement: Let X/R be smooth proper geometrically integral of dimension d≥3, and assume CH₀(X_C′) is supported on a surface for every algebraically closed extension C′ containing R. In dimension 3 the left side is H³_nr(X,Q/Z(2))_0, classes whose restriction at every real point vanishes.

conventions.geometry: Unless an item explicitly admits proper nonprojective varieties, X/k is smooth projective of pure dimension d. Rational Chow groups mean integral Chow groups tensored with Q; equality in a realization never means equality in CH. Geometrically integral hypotheses are stated where used.
conventions.coefficients: For the standard conjectures, k is algebraically closed, H is a fixed classical Weil cohomology with characteristic-zero coefficient field F, and hard Lefschetz for H is an input. A_H^i is the Q-span of rational algebraic classes in H^{2i}(X)(i). Positivity is on this rational space, never an order on Q_l. Scalar extensions are separate interfaces.
conventions.hodge: The untwisted class of a codimension-p cycle has Hodge type (p,p) in weight 2p. After twist (p) it has type (0,0). Tau Ceti uses weight -2m and type (-m,-m) for its Tate object tate m. Rational and integral Hodge conjectures are separate predicates.
conventions.real: R denotes a specified real closed field, C=R(i), G=Gal(C/R). The notation real numbers means the Archimedean field. For general R use equivariant semialgebraic cohomology; do not postulate an analytic Hodge decomposition. Z(j) has G-action (-1)^j. Identifications of embedded twist lattices used by different authors require a scalar normalization.
conventions.S3: X/R is smooth proper geometrically integral, d>=1. The real-locus pairing is total cup-product degree H^{d-1}(X(R),F2) x H^1(X(R),F2) -> F2; no orientation is needed.
conventions.S54: S3, plus either R is the real numbers or H^2(X,O_X)=0, real integral Hodge for 1-cycles, and universal CH0 support on a surface after every algebraically closed extension C/R. Low-dimensional statements use the source zero conventions; d>=3 is imposed for cohomology indexed d-3.
conventions.status: Conjecture predicates, conditional implication theorems, proof-scoped proved cases, source-only register entries, and source questions are labelled separately in each target. An unchecked planning node is never a library implementation.
